summary.headline: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 3.2% YoY to ₹238.16 crore, but EBITDA fell to ₹27.73 crore (11.6% margin) on energy and freight costs.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations grew 3.2% YoY to ₹238.16 crore, a return to YoY growth, though down from ₹244.72 crore in Q1 FY27. Gross margin was stable at 47.7% versus 47.6% a year ago. EBITDA fell to ₹27.73 crore from ₹31.85 crore YoY and ₹35.87 crore QoQ, with margin at 11.6%, as higher furnace oil, gas and freight costs weighed. PAT was ₹13.64 crore and PBT ₹19.20 crore, both below prior-year and prior-quarter levels. Management said H2 should be similar to or better than H1 but declined to give numerical guidance.

segments.name: Paints
segments.commentary: Largest market but did not grow YoY in Q2 because of subdued demand; management says paint customers raised prices three times in six months and their margins were squeezed.

segments.name: Polymers, rubber, construction chemicals and other non-paint markets
segments.commentary: Non-paint markets now above half of sales; management says it grew in double digits with polymer, rubber and construction-chemical customers in Q2.

segments.name: 20 Microns Nano
segments.commentary: Grew in double digits in Q2 with higher profitability, per management; functional additives (250+ grades) are about one quarter of revenue.

segments.name: Minford (mineral-based organic fertiliser)
segments.commentary: Small contributor to revenue; focus on India and parts of Africa, with state-level licensing in progress.

guidance_outlook: Management says the 18% CAGR is in place with the projects and mining reserves, but did not give a numerical FY27 revenue or margin range given market uncertainty.
H2 FY27 should be 'similar to better' than H1 if Q2 conditions persist; management said H2 will 'definitely be better than H1'.
Q3 volumes are expected to run in line with Q2 until the festival season ends; demand uptick expected after that and Q4 is seasonally strongest.

Solar (9 MW) targeted for Q4 FY27 commissioning, expected to meet about 40% of power needs and deliver about ₹8 crore annual EBITDA benefit (about 80 bps), with full benefit from FY28/FY29 (call remarks vary).
Captive talc (Andhra Pradesh) and quartz/feldspar (Rajasthan) mines expected to start production from December 2026.
Malaysia quarry capacity to rise from 4,000 MT to 8,000 MT by FY29, with plant commissioning by FY30.
No buyback planned; promoter stake increase discussed but no timeline given.
capex_capacity: ₹100 crore CapEx programme: about ₹30 crore deployed so far (₹12 crore captive solar, ₹7 crore two mine acquisitions); ₹17 crore more planned in Q3, all on solar, taking deployment to nearly half. Management said remaining ~70% to be deployed over 15-18 months; funded by internal accruals and selective debt.
Captive solar: 9 MW across 5.5 MW Rajasthan and 3.5 MW Gujarat, total investment about ₹29 crore, targeted for Q4 FY27 commissioning.
Capacity additions planned in calcium carbonate, engineered kaolin, talc and nano functional additives over the next two to three years.

Advanced materials: graphite produced internally on a small scale; high-purity quartz in development; bid placed under India's REPM PLI scheme (about 20 bidders), results expected in a couple of months.
demand_pricing: Pricing is case by case: management said it can pass through exceptional power or fuel hikes for some customers, but in highly competitive products competitors are not raising prices.
Raw-material and freight costs rose sharply due to import dependence; imports are about 40% of raw material (China, Malaysia, Vietnam), local sourcing about 60%.
No order book disclosed; customers give fixed quarterly volumes, which management said are unchanged for Q3 and will grow in Q4.
Export freight rose; freight per MT went from ₹2,108 to ₹2,346 QoQ.
Management attributed the gap between customer revenue growth (double digits, on retail price hikes) and its own growth to its B2B pricing and product mix.

qa_highlights.question: Why has 20 Microns' sales growth lagged its paint, polymer and pipe customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said customer financials do not map directly; customers raised retail prices, but 20 Microns cannot pass the same increases. Polymer, rubber and construction-chemical customers grew double digits in Q2, while paint customers did not grow due to subdued demand.

qa_highlights.question: Are there plans for buybacks or a promoter stake increase?
qa_highlights.answer: No buyback plans as of now. A promoter stake increase is discussed regularly and is one area management will look at 'in the near future'.

qa_highlights.question: What were the H1 cost increases for furnace oil, gas and freight, and what does the solar benefit depend on?
qa_highlights.answer: Furnace oil rose from about ₹42/kg to ₹56/kg (+33%, ₹1.34 crore); gas from ₹69 to ₹122/kg (+77%, ₹0.62 crore); freight per MT from ₹2,108 to ₹2,346 (+11%, ₹2.92 crore). Total ₹4.78 crore, about 200 bps. Solar grid tariff is about ₹3.45–3.5 net of O&M, per the CFO's answer.

qa_highlights.question: What is the H2 margin and revenue outlook, and how much of the 18% CAGR starts when?
qa_highlights.answer: No numerical range given. Management said H2 will be better than H1 if Q2 conditions hold and the 18% CAGR is supported by projects and mines, with the 70% remaining capex deployed over 15-18 months.

qa_highlights.question: How are value-added products performing, and what is their margin contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said specialty products have started to contribute to margins; Nano grew in double digits with higher profit, but raw-material and freight costs offset gains. Margins should improve once these costs stabilise.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Q3 and what is the order book?
qa_highlights.answer: No order book is disclosed. Q3 is expected to run like Q2 until the festival season ends; Q4 is typically the strongest quarter.

risks_watch: EBITDA margin compression from energy (furnace oil, gas) and freight costs; management has not quantified the recovery path.
Import dependence (about 40% of raw material) exposes costs to USD pricing and freight; supply chain disruptions cited.
Paint segment demand remains subdued; price-competitive products limit pass-through of cost increases.
Working-capital and cash-flow catch-up expected as inventory normalises; not yet visible in numbers.
Execution risk on ₹100 crore capex, solar commissioning in Q4 and mine start-up from December 2026.
Pending PLI result for rare-earth permanent magnets; high-purity quartz and graphite are early-stage with no timelines disclosed.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term structure (durable specified grades, captive raw materials, solar) but cautious and non-numerical on near-term margins and FY27 outlook, citing unpredictable markets, energy costs and supply-chain disruption. Several answers deferred to the IR team, including the order-book split and opacifier share.
key_quotes: Revenue growth returned in the second quarter and our gross margin for the half rose by about 80 basis points.
A new grade typically takes anywhere from three to ten years to move from the first brief to commercial supply.
Once running, solar should meet about 40% of our power needs.
But there are no plans for a buyback as of now.

growth.why: Management gave no numeric FY27 revenue guidance, only that H2 should be similar to better than H1 with Q4 seasonally strongest, backed by captive mines (Dec 2026 start), 9 MW solar (Q4 FY27) and ~₹30 cr of the ₹100 cr capex deployed, while paint demand stays subdued and no order book is disclosed.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin fell to 11.6% (from 13.8% ex the ₹4.78 cr energy and freight hit, and 15.0% in Q1 FY27 at ₹35.87 cr on ₹244.72 cr); recovery depends on energy and freight costs easing and solar (~80 bps, ~₹8 cr/yr) arriving, with no numerical margin guidance.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Captive mines (talc in Andhra Pradesh, quartz/feldspar in Rajasthan) start production from Dec 2026 and 9 MW solar is targeted for Q4 FY27; Malaysia quarry goes from 4,000 to 8,000 MT by FY29, but these are mainly raw-material and power capacity rather than new product-line capacity.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q3 volumes guided flat to Q2 until festival season ends, with Q4 seasonally strongest and volumes to grow; Q2 revenue was +3.2% YoY, and paint demand is subdued (no growth in Q2) while non-paint markets grew double digits.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Only about ₹30 cr of the ₹100 cr programme is deployed (~30%), with ₹17 cr more in Q3 and the remaining ~70% over 15-18 months, plus capacity additions planned in calcium carbonate, kaolin, talc and nano additives over 2-3 years; utilisation not disclosed, so the case is driven by the programme rather than a utilisation trigger.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No numerical guidance was given; management only said H2 would be similar to better than H1, while Q2 EBITDA fell to ₹27.73 cr from ₹35.87 cr QoQ and energy and freight costs remain elevated.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Energy (furnace oil +33%, gas +77%) and freight (+11%/MT) cost ₹4.78 cr in H1 (~200 bps), paint demand is subdued after customers raised prices three times in six months, and the H2 outlook is conditional on Q2 conditions persisting.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No specific new product launch timed in the call; capacity additions in functional additives are planned over 2-3 years, and high-purity quartz and graphite have no timelines.

rows.label: Energy and freight cost normalisation
rows.why: Furnace oil ₹42→₹56/kg, gas ₹69→₹122/kg and freight ₹2,108→₹2,346/MT cost ₹4.78 cr in H1; margin recovers only if these ease, and management has not quantified a recovery path.

rows.label: Captive solar 9 MW commissioning
rows.why: ₹29 cr investment across 5.5 MW Rajasthan and 3.5 MW Gujarat, meeting ~40% of power needs and worth ~₹8 cr annual EBITDA (~80 bps) at full run-rate from FY28/FY29; grid tariff ~₹3.45–3.5 net of O&M.

rows.label: Working-capital release as inventory normalises
rows.why: Management expects working-capital and cash-flow catch-up as inventory normalises, but it is not yet visible in the numbers and no amount was given.
